response.sql:
WITH channel_avg AS (
  SELECT o.orderbase AS channel, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_rate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL AND o.orderbase IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.orderbase
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS bench FROM channel_avg
),
above AS (
  SELECT c.avg_rate, c.avg_rate - b.bench AS excess
  FROM channel_avg c
  CROSS JOIN benchmark b
  WHERE c.avg_rate > b.bench
)
SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS mean_avg_rate,
       AVG(excess) AS mean_excess_over_benchmark
FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: Each fee row counts equally within its channel: a channel's average is the AVG of feerate over all fee rows whose linked order has that orderbase, so an order with several fee rows contributes several values.
Fee rows with NULL feerate are excluded, as the request specifies. Fee rows whose order has no orderbase (NULL channel) are also excluded, since they cannot be assigned to a channel.
Fee rows with no matching order are dropped by the inner join, and a channel with no non-null feerate values produces no average and so is not part of the benchmark.

alternatives.interpretation: Average the fee rate per order first, then average those per-order values within each channel, so every order has equal weight regardless of how many fee rows it has. The benchmark and above-benchmark steps are the same.
alternatives.sql:
WITH order_avg AS (
  SELECT o.recordvault, o.orderbase AS channel, AVG(f.feerate) AS order_rate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL AND o.orderbase IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.recordvault, o.orderbase
),
channel_avg AS (
  SELECT channel, AVG(order_rate) AS avg_rate
  FROM order_avg
  GROUP BY channel
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS bench FROM channel_avg
),
above AS (
  SELECT c.avg_rate, c.avg_rate - b.bench AS excess
  FROM channel_avg c
  CROSS JOIN benchmark b
  WHERE c.avg_rate > b.bench
)
SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS mean_avg_rate,
       AVG(excess) AS mean_excess_over_benchmark
FROM above;
